input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the per-chunk debug line logs chunks[0].score for every rank instead of chunk.score
- failure path: debug mode prints the same score for every retrieved chunk; whoever reads the log to tune the threshold sees ranks 2..k with the top score and draws the wrong conclusion

Reviewer finding
- description: The per-chunk debug log prints chunks[0].score for every rank instead of the score of the chunk being logged.
- rationale: Trigger: retrieval returns several chunks with different scores. Mechanism: the loop variable is `chunk`, but the format argument is `chunks[0].score`, so every line reports the top chunk's score under a different rank and page. Impact: operators reading debug logs see misleading relevance scores when diagnosing retrieval and abstention behavior.
critique: The finding pins down the same faulty operation: the per-chunk debug log uses chunks[0].score instead of the loop variable chunk's score, so every rank shows the top score. It also gives the same consequence of misleading scores for anyone diagnosing retrieval from the logs.
